description: The party-affiliation legends printed in each section of Walker's 1918-92 volume, and the sources each section states it was compiled from. The codes are how the volume labels a candidate's party; reading a harvested figure's party needs the legend of the section it came from, because the same code differs between sections (R is Republican in both Belfast and Dublin sections, but SF, Lab and Ind carry section-specific conventions). Transcribed from the scans and checked by eye; OCR noise corrected against the page image.

provenance.method: OCR of the Introduction and abbreviations pages (printed pp. 3, 13-14, 43-44, 99-100, 279-280), then every legend re-read against the page image

source.title: Parliamentary Election Results in Ireland, 1918-92
source.publisher: Royal Irish Academy and the Institute of Irish Studies, Queen's University of Belfast

provenance.licence: Facts only: abbreviation codes, the party names they stand for, and bibliographic entries. No prose from the volume is reproduced; the notes below paraphrase it.

conventions.Ind: Independent. Placed before a party designation (Ind U, Ind N) it marks an unofficial candidate of that party.
conventions.firstPreferences: For elections held by single transferable vote the votes shown are first preferences; the quota and the order of election are recorded.
conventions.unionistLabels: From 1969 the volume distinguishes unionist candidates by stance: U (O'N) official candidates supporting Terence O'Neill, O'N U independent pro-O'Neill unionists, U (P) or U (Pro A) candidates in 1973-4 supporting the Assembly and power-sharing. The Ulster Unionist Party is labelled OUP (Official Unionist Party) from October 1974. In the 1974 general elections and the 1975 Convention election, OUP, DUP and VUP candidates stood under the joint United Ulster Unionist Council label, and entries give both party and UUUC endorsement.
